title: Temporary Total Ratings for Hospitalization and Convalescence (Disability Compensation)
content:
**When it is assigned.** A temporary total rating is assigned on a Disability Compensation award when a service-connected disability required hospitalization for more than the hospitalization threshold in days, or surgery or treatment requiring convalescence.

**What it pays and for how long.** It is paid at the temporary total monthly rate from the first day of hospitalization or the date of surgery, and ends on the last day of the month of discharge or of the convalescence period.

**Convalescence length.** An initial convalescence period runs for 1 month up to the initial maximum, and it can be extended by no more than the extension maximum of further months in total.

**When it ends.** When it ends, the prior combined rating resumes without a reduction proposal.

**Questions answered by the rule**

*Does a hospitalization of exactly the threshold number of days qualify?* No; the hospitalization must last more than that number of days. With the 21-day threshold of the Disability Compensation temporary total schedule, 21 days does not qualify and 22 days does.

*When does a temporary total rating that began with surgery on 9 October, with a three-month convalescence period ending on 8 January, stop?* On 31 January, the last day of the month in which the convalescence period ends (hypothetical dates).

*Is a reduction proposal sent when the temporary total rating ends?* No. The prior combined rating simply resumes.

*How far can convalescence be extended?* By no more than the extension maximum in total, however many extensions are granted.
